valid.name: a method signature makes the interface a contract
a lone readonly property with fewer than 3 mutable-data siblings remains sufficient contract evidence
every property readonly is a genuine immutability contract regardless of property count
a toString overload with parameters is a genuine method, not the builtin-shadow decoy shape

invalid.name: index-only data has no contract signal
generic pure data has no contract signal
a named pure-data reference carries no contract signal
a throwaway parameterless toString(): string decoy does not rescue an otherwise pure-data interface
a lone readonly property among 3 or more plain mutable-data properties is not sufficient contract evidence
